_doc: THE single per-SKU peak source for GEAK. Every consumer READS this file and none carries a copy: kernel_workflow/scripts/kernel_tools/{hw_budget,calc_perf,mem_bw_probe,extract_sku}.py (calc_perf.SKU_PEAKS is built from it at import), e2e_workflow/knowledge/analysis_skills/roofline/roofline_tools.py (product rows by gpu_identity `sku`, then `target`, else the row flagged roofline_default_for_arch), and every markdown copy of these numbers, which is a GENERATED block (e2e .../roofline/peaks.md, kernel_workflow/knowledge/amd_instinct.md, perf_knowledge/hardware/cdna{3,4}_*/peak_tables.md, the pack's references/hardware/amd-*-skus.md + atlas.md) rendered by `extract_sku.py --sync-docs` and checked by `extract_sku.py --check-docs` / the tests. Edit a number HERE (with its source), run `extract_sku.py --check && extract_sku.py --sync-docs`, then the tests. Row order: gfx950 first (the main line), then gfx942, then the client parts GEAK validates, then rows kept for reference only (geak_support=unsupported). peak_tflops = dense (no sparsity) matrix-engine rates (MFMA on CDNA, WMMA on RDNA); fp32 on RDNA rows is the dual-issue VALU rate (RDNA has no fp32 WMMA); peak_tflops_vector = datasheet VALU rates where they differ in meaning. A dtype absent from peak_tflops has NO rate: consumers refuse or report unknown, never substitute fp16. bf16 == fp16 on every row (same matrix-core rate) and every dtype:fp16 ratio is constant within one arch (hw_budget --selftest asserts both). basis (compute): datasheet | derived (published clock x CU x per-CU rate; basis_note says how) | orc-derived (estimate, no public datasheet). peak_hbm_basis: datasheet | measured (then datasheet_hbm_tb_s carries the pin rate and measured_ceilings names tool + version). clock_mhz only where sourced. source = where the row's numbers come from. Every '% of roofline' computed against these numbers carries denominator_basis=datasheet (or the measured tool) and may RANK, never gate or close -- only a measured numerator over a probed/calibrated denominator may gate (see perf_knowledge/profiling/roofline_on_mi.md).

_schema.identity_target: scripts/gpu_identity.py `sku` value that selects this row (`r9700` is also that identity's `target`; Instinct rows are reached through `sku` only -- `target` stays r9700 | unknown). null = no product identity; reached only through the arch default or --sku
_schema.geak_support: supported | unsupported (kept for reference; never an arch default)
_schema.roofline_default_for_arch: true on exactly one supported row per arch that may be used when only the gfx is known (gfx950->MI355X, gfx942->MI300X, gfx1151->AI_MAX_395); gfx1201 has none ON PURPOSE (R9700 peaks are product-scoped)
_schema.cus: physical CUs (rocminfo Compute Unit, full device, unpartitioned)
_schema.clock_mhz: sourced clocks only (null = not sourced here)
_schema.l2_mb: aggregate L2 (= l2_per_xcd_mb x xcds on CDNA)
_schema.peak_hbm_tb_s: the external-memory ceiling consumers divide by
_schema.datasheet_hbm_tb_s: pin rate, present when peak_hbm_basis != datasheet
_schema.peak_tflops: dense matrix-engine TFLOP/s (TOPS for int); absent dtype = no rate
_schema.basis_note: how a derived number was derived
_schema.measured_ceilings: [{metric, value, tool, tool_version, source}] -- empirical ceilings; a denominator taken from one is empirical@tool-version

_no_derived_ridge: The ridge (ops/byte at which the compute and memory ceilings cross) is NOT stored here, and must not be re-added. It is peak_tflops[dtype] / peak_hbm_tb_s, so it is a different number for every dtype -- on MI325X it is 218 at fp16, 436 at fp8 and 27 at fp32. A stored ridge is a cache of that division taken at ONE dtype, and it WAS read back for every dtype, which put every fp32 kernel with an intensity between 27 and 218 on the wrong side of the crossover. hw_budget.py computes it per call from the dtype's own peak.
_lds_doc: lds_per_cu_kib is null on every RDNA row ON PURPOSE, and must not be refilled with 64. RDNA shared memory is a per-WGP pool and a WGP is 2 CUs, so a per-CU figure is not a smaller true quantity -- it is a quantity that does not exist at that granularity: two workgroups landing on the same WGP contend for ONE 128 KiB pool, not for two independent 64s. The old 64.0 was 128/2, arithmetically defensible and therefore undetectable on inspection -- it is also exactly gfx942's genuine per-CU figure, so an RDNA reading was numerically indistinguishable from a CDNA3 one. Three distinct quantities live in hw_constants.json and must never be collapsed into one 'LDS size': lds_per_cu_kib (CDNA, the per-CU pool), lds_per_wgp_kib (RDNA, the per-WGP pool -- this is the OCCUPANCY pool), and lds_per_wg_kib (RDNA, the per-workgroup allocation limit, 64 KiB). Read the RDNA two from hw_constants.json and name which one you used; consumers that cannot must report occupancy as not priced rather than divide by 2.

MI355X.source: AMD Instinct MI355X data sheet / product page (dense, no sparsity): FP16/BF16 2.5 PF, FP8 5.0 PF, MXFP6/MXFP4 10 PF, INT8 5.0 POPS, FP32 157.3 TF, FP64 78.6 TF (vector = matrix), 288 GB HBM3E 8.0 TB/s, 256 CU, 2400 MHz peak engine clock, 256 MB Infinity Cache; L2 4 MB per XCD x 8 XCD (AMD CDNA4 architecture whitepaper).

MI350X.source: AMD Instinct MI350X data sheet / product page (dense): FP16/BF16 2.3 PF, FP8 4.6 PF, MXFP6/MXFP4 9.2 PF, INT8 4.6 POPS, FP32 144.2 TF, FP64 72.1 TF, 288 GB HBM3E 8.0 TB/s, 256 CU, 2200 MHz peak engine clock (lower clock/TBP than MI355X -- same silicon, different peaks; never copy MI355X numbers here).

MI300X.source: AMD Instinct MI300X data sheet (dense): FP16/BF16 1307.4 TF, FP8 2614.9 TF, INT8 2614.9 TOPS, FP32 163.4 TF (vector and matrix), FP64 matrix 163.4 / vector 81.7 TF, 192 GB HBM3 5.3 TB/s, 304 CU, 2100 MHz peak engine clock, 256 MB Infinity Cache; L2 4 MB per XCD x 8 (AMD CDNA3 whitepaper).

MI325X.source: AMD Instinct MI325X data sheet: compute identical to MI300X (same 304-CU gfx942 die, 2100 MHz); 256 GB HBM3E at 6.0 TB/s (NOT MI300X's 5.3).

MI308X.source: No public global datasheet. Matrix peaks scaled from MI300X by CU count (80/304 at the MI300X per-CU rate); HBM and cache figures carried from the pack's amd-cdna3-skus.md (ORC-derived). Rank only; calibrate before any gate.

R9700.source: AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 specifications (dense; sparse 2:4 is 2x and is NOT tabulated): FP16/BF16 191 TF, FP8 383 TF, INT8 383 TOPS, INT4 766 TOPS, FP32 vector 47.8 TF; 32 GB GDDR6 256-bit at 20 Gbps = 640 GB/s; 64 MB Infinity Cache, 8 MB L2; 1620 base / 2350 game / 2920 boost MHz. No fp4 / block-scaled MX path. Product-scoped: a bare gfx1201 must NOT inherit this row.

measured_ceilings.tool: torch copy_ event-timed, 1 GiB src + 1 GiB dst, 30 copies (GEAK)

AI_MAX_395.basis_note: fp16/bf16/int8 = 512 ops/clk/CU (WMMA) x 40 CU x 2.9 GHz = 59.4; int4 = 1024 ops/clk/CU x 40 x 2.9 = 118.8 (RDNA3-family IU4 WMMA runs at 2x the IU8 rate -- the same 2:1 AMD publishes for gfx1100, RX 7900 XTX 123 -> 246 TOPS; the old 59.4 had no source and sat on the dangerous, too-low side); fp32 = 256 FLOP/clk/CU (dual-issue VOPD / wave64 FMA, the same convention as the RX7900XTX 61.4 TF row) x 40 x 2.9 GHz = 29.7 (14.85 without dual issue). The old 20.0 had no source and broke the per-arch fp32:fp16 = 0.5 ratio every other RDNA3 row satisfies.
AI_MAX_395.source: AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 product page / blog (40 CU Radeon 8060S, 2.9 GHz, LPDDR5X-8000 256-bit = 256 GB/s pin rate); 2 MB L2 + 32 MB Infinity Cache (MALL) per the AMD RDNA3.5 Strix Halo disclosure; 212 GB/s is MEASURED (see measured_ceilings), not a datasheet figure.

measured_ceilings.source: llm-tracker.info AMD Strix Halo GPU performance page (404 as of 2026; figure retained in the pack's amd-rdna35-skus.md)

AI_MAX_495.basis_note: same per-CU rates as AI_MAX_395 at 3.0 GHz: 512 x 40 x 3.0 = 61.4 (fp16/bf16/int8); int4 1024 x 40 x 3.0 = 122.9; fp32 256 x 40 x 3.0 = 30.7.
AI_MAX_495.source: AMD Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495 product page + AMD Gorgon Halo blog (40 CU, 3.0 GHz Radeon 8065S, LPDDR5X-8533 x 256-bit = 273 GB/s theoretical, not yet measured). Same gfx1151 die as 395 -> same L2/MALL.

_mall_doc: mall_mb = the MEMORY-SIDE last-level cache (AMD Infinity Cache), which sits behind the Infinity Fabric and is NOT l2_mb: l2_mb is the aggregate of the per-XCD L2s (l2_per_xcd_mb x xcds on CDNA; each XCD's CUs see only their own slice) and is the GATEWAY onto the fabric. This distinction decides two things. (1) Every TCC/EA counter (TCC_MISS, FETCH_SIZE, WRITE_SIZE, EA RDREQ/WRREQ) is measured at the L2/fabric boundary, so it counts FABRIC traffic; whether a byte came from this cache or from HBM is invisible to all of them. (2) A bandwidth ceiling probe or a kernel measurement is only about HBM once the footprint clears THIS capacity, not l2_mb -- clearing 4x the L2 while sitting inside the memory-side cache measures cache and calls it DRAM, which biases the ceiling HIGH and every gap derived from it LOW. null = not established for this SKU; treat the residency bar as unknown, not as l2_mb. Source: AMD CDNA4 architecture whitepaper (memory hierarchy / Infinity Cache section).
